newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: TAIWAN CPC SEES OVER T$6 BLN LOSS ON CURRENCY FALL.
newsitem.headline: TAIWAN CPC SEES OVER T$6 BLN LOSS ON CURRENCY FALL.

text.p: Taiwan's state oil monopoly Chinese Petroleum Corp is expected to lose more than T$6 billion in the current fiscal year 1997/1998 (July-June) if the Taiwan dollar continues to fall, a company official said on Thursday.

The Taiwan dollar has been tumbling drastically over the past two weeks, hitting a nine-year low last Wednesday after the central bank allowed it to fall below T$28 to the U.S. dollar for the first time since 1989.
"...We can expect to lose T$6 billion in the next 12 months if the currency exchange losses stay," the company official said.
At midday on Thursday, the Taiwan dollar hit a new nine-year low of T$28.84 and was testing T$29.00.
"It is nearly T$1.50 lower," the official said when asked to comment on the latest plunge. "At this rate, the losses will be greater."
CPC buys its crude in U.S. dollars, so with each plunge in the local currency, the crude costs more.
But the official said CPC would not raise domestic oil product prices for the time being as the currency losses were being offset by lower crude prices.
